# Review of FDS Section 6.2 Tank Pressure Control

Defects D-04, D-06 and D-07 are safety-relevant. As written, the high-high trip stops the equipment that relieves the tank, the trip can be bypassed from the HMI, and nothing protects the tank from vacuum.

## Defect list

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-01 | 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3, 6.2.6 | Setpoints (120, 220, 250, 290, -5) are in prose. The setpoint list is not the single source of truth. | Move all values to the setpoint list. Refer to them by ID. |
| D-02 | 6.2.1 | PV source, output, action, modes and load-sharing of PIC-501 are not defined. "Capacity" has no method. Duty/standby and lead/lag for K-501A/B are not defined. | Add a regulatory control section with a lead/lag rule. |
| D-03 | 6.2.2 | PIC-510 is not defined as modulating or on/off. Close or reseat behavior is missing. The fail position of PV-512 and the flare availability rule are missing. | Define PIC-510 as a separate controller with its own setpoint. Define the PV-512 fail position and the behavior when the flare is not proven. |
| D-04 | 6.2.3 | **Hazardous logic.** Tripping K-501A/B at high-high tank pressure removes the main pressure relief path. Pressure then rises toward the PSV set pressure. "To protect them" is a compressor-protection reason and belongs to the vendor trips. | Do not trip the compressors on tank high-high. Hold them at maximum load. Define the tank high-high action in the SRS. |
| D-05 | 6.2.3 | The high-high is a safety function, but the document does not say whether the BPCS or the SIS does it. Latching, reset and SIL are missing. | Reference the SIF in the SRS. State what the BPCS does at high-high (alarm, maximum load). |
| D-06 | 6.2.4 | An HMI bypass of a safety trip removes a protection layer. It has no authorization, no time limit and no alarm. | Remove it. The BPCS has no write path to any SIS trip. Any bypass uses a hardwired method under the site bypass procedure and the SRS. |
| D-07 | 6.2.5 | "Low pressure is not a concern" is false. The compressors can pull the tank to vacuum, and the vacuum relief valve is set only just below atmospheric. There is no low alarm, low-low trip, minimum load or make-up gas. | Add low and low-low pressure functions, a minimum-load rule and an open item for a make-up gas source. |
| D-08 | 6.2.5 | "Run continuously" conflicts with duty/standby operation of K-501A/B. Start, stop, changeover and restart are not defined. | Add the state table, the start and stop sequences and the restart rules. |
| D-09 | 6.2.5 | "Is not a concern" cannot be tested. | Replace it with testable requirements (FR-TPC-020 to FR-TPC-024). |
| D-10 | 6.2.6 | PSV and vacuum relief set pressures are relief design data, not control logic. There is no reference to the relief datasheet. The setpoint order is not checked. | List the values in the setpoint list as given data. Add an order check. |
| D-11 | 6.2.7 | "Provided by the vendor package" is a reference, not a specification. The interface signals and the failure responses are missing. "Anti-surge" implies a centrifugal compressor, which is unusual at this scale. | Define the interface signals and the BPCS response. Add an open item to confirm the compressor type. |
| D-12 | All | There are no requirement IDs and no test methods. | Assign FR-TPC-NNN IDs with a test method for each. |
| D-13 | All | Bad PV, comms loss, power loss and restart, and fail positions are missing. Transmitter tags are missing. | Add an abnormal handling section with two transmitters. |
| D-14 | All | Alarms, operator interface and open items are missing. | Add them. |
| D-15 | 6.2.1, 6.2.2 | The control transmitters are not separated from the safety transmitters. | Require independent SIS transmitters in the SRS. The BPCS uses PT-501A/B only. |

## Corrected section

### 6.2 Tank Pressure Control

**6.2.1 Purpose and boundaries**

FR-TPC-001: This section covers vapor space pressure control of the LNG tank. It uses BOG compressors K-501A/B and flare control valve PV-512. (Test: inspection)

The upstream interface is the tank vapor line. The downstream interfaces are the BOG header and the flare. K-501A/B come as vendor packages. SIS functions are in the SRS and are not specified here.

**6.2.2 Equipment and tags**

| Tag | Description | Note |
|---|---|---|
| PT-501A, PT-501B | Tank pressure transmitters for the BPCS | Provisional tags, confirm (OI-08) |
| PIC-501 | Compressor load controller | |
| PIC-510 | Flare pressure controller | |
| PV-512 | Tank vapor to flare control valve | |
| K-501A, K-501B | BOG compressors | |

**6.2.3 Setpoint list**

| ID | Item | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | PIC-501 setpoint | 120 | mbarg | Given |
| SP-02 | PIC-510 setpoint | 220 | mbarg | Given |
| SP-03 | Tank pressure high alarm (PAH) | 180 | mbarg | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-04 | Tank pressure high-high alarm and SIS trip (PAHH) | 250 | mbarg | Given |
| SP-05 | Tank PSV set pressure | 290 | mbarg | Given |
| SP-06 | Tank pressure low alarm (PAL) | 80 | mbarg | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-07 | Tank pressure low-low (PALL) compressor trip | 40 | mbarg | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-08 | Vacuum relief valve set pressure | -5 | mbarg | Given |
| SP-09 | Lag compressor start, PIC-501 output | 90 | % | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-10 | Lag compressor stop, PIC-501 output | 40 | % | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-11 | PT-501A/B deviation alarm | 15 | mbar | Provisional, confirm |
| SP-12 | Compressor minimum load | 25 | % | Provisional, confirm with vendor |
| SP-13 | PV-512 open alarm threshold | 5 | % | Provisional, confirm |

Order check: SP-08 < SP-07 < SP-06 < SP-01 < SP-03 < SP-02 < SP-04 < SP-05. This order is correct.

| ID | Timer | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-01 | Lag start delay | 60 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-02 | Lag stop delay | 600 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-03 | Permissive check | 10 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-04 | Running feedback | 60 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-05 | Unload to minimum load | 120 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-06 | Stopped feedback | 60 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-07 | PT deviation delay | 10 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-08 | Anti-surge active alarm delay | 60 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-09 | PV-512 open alarm delay | 30 | s | Provisional, confirm |
| T-10 | Serial comms loss detection | 5 | s | Provisional, confirm |

**6.2.4 States and transitions (K-501A/B)**

| From | To | Condition | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stopped | Starting | All start permissives true | Operator (lead), BPCS (lag, per FR-TPC-013) | Operator-prompted (lead), automatic (lag) |
| Starting | Running | Running feedback true within T-04 | BPCS | Automatic |
| Starting | Tripped | T-04 expires, or trip signal | BPCS | Automatic |
| Running | Stopping | Stop command, or lag stop per FR-TPC-013 | Operator, BPCS | Operator-prompted (lead), automatic (lag) |
| Running | Tripped | PALL, vendor trip, or power loss | BPCS, vendor package | Automatic |
| Stopping | Stopped | Stopped feedback true within T-06 | BPCS | Automatic |
| Stopping | Tripped | T-06 expires | BPCS | Automatic |
| Tripped | Stopped | Trip cause clear and operator RESET | Operator | Manual |

Start permissives for each compressor:
- No latched trip.
- Vendor package ready.
- PV above SP-07.
- No serial comms fault.

**6.2.5 Regulatory control**

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-TPC-010 | The BPCS uses the higher of PT-501A and PT-501B as the PV for PIC-501, PIC-510 and the high alarms. It uses the lower for the low alarms and PALL. | FAT: simulate both transmitters |
| FR-TPC-011 | PIC-501 PV is the selected tank pressure. Setpoint is SP-01. Output is load demand to the running compressors. Action is direct: output rises as pressure rises. Modes are Auto and Manual. There is no cascade. | FAT: step test |
| FR-TPC-012 | Running compressors share the load demand equally. The load demand never goes below SP-12 while a compressor runs. | FAT: simulate |
| FR-TPC-013 | The operator selects the lead compressor. The BPCS starts the lag compressor when PIC-501 output stays above SP-09 for T-01. It stops the lag compressor when the output stays below SP-10 for T-02. | FAT: simulate output |
| FR-TPC-014 | If the lead compressor trips, the BPCS starts the lag compressor at once if permissives are true. | FAT: trip lead |
| FR-TPC-015 | PIC-510 PV is the selected tank pressure. Setpoint is SP-02. Output is the PV-512 position. Action is direct. PV-512 stays closed below SP-02. The controller has anti-windup. There is no cascade. | FAT: ramp PV |
| FR-TPC-016 | PIC-510 opens PV-512 whether or not the flare is proven. If the flare is not proven, the BPCS raises an alarm. | FAT: simulate flare fault |
| FR-TPC-017 | The BPCS keeps PIC-510 in Auto. A change to Manual needs engineer access level and raises an alarm. | FAT: access test |

**6.2.6 Sequences**

Start K-501 (SqBC):

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check start permissives | All true | T-03 | End start. Show the failed permissive. Raise alarm. |
| 2 | Send start command to vendor package | Running feedback true | T-04 | Send stop command. Go to Tripped. Raise alarm. |
| 3 | Hold load demand at SP-12, then release to PIC-501 | Vendor ready to load | T-03 | Hold at SP-12. Raise alarm. |

Stop K-501 (SqBC):

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ramp load demand to SP-12 | Load feedback at SP-12 | T-05 | Go to step 2. Raise alarm. |
| 2 | Send stop command to vendor package | Stopped feedback true | T-06 | Go to Tripped. Raise alarm. Prompt: "Use local stop on K-501." |

**6.2.7 Interlocks and permissives**

| ID | Cause | Effect | Latched or auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IL-01 | PV above SP-04 (PAHH) | Set load demand to maximum. Keep PIC-510 in Auto. Do not trip the compressors. SIS actions are in the SRS. | Alarm latched | Operator acknowledge after PV below SP-03 |
| IL-02 | PV below SP-07 (PALL) | Trip all running K-501. Stop lag start. | Latched | Operator RESET after PV above SP-06 |
| IL-03 | Vendor common trip | Compressor goes to Tripped. Lag starts per FR-TPC-014. | Latched | Operator RESET at faceplate after vendor reset |
| IL-04 | Both PT-501A/B bad | See FR-TPC-030. | Auto-reset | Auto when one transmitter is good |

FR-TPC-020: The BPCS has no write path from the HMI to any SIS trip, and no BPCS bypass of IL-01 or IL-02. Any SIS bypass uses a hardwired method under the SRS and the site bypass procedure. (Test: inspection, FAT)

FR-TPC-021: IL-02 acts at the BPCS level and operates in addition to any SIF in the SRS. (Test: FAT)

FR-TPC-022: The BPCS never trips a K-501 compressor on tank high or high-high pressure. (Test: FAT, simulate PAHH)

**6.2.8 Alarms**

Priorities are provisional. Confirm them in the alarm database under ISA-18.2.

| Alarm | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| PAH | PV above SP-03 | Medium | Check the compressor load. Check for ship unloading. |
| PAHH | PV above SP-04 | High | Start the high-pressure response procedure. |
| PAL | PV below SP-06 | Medium | Check the compressor load and the make-up source. |
| PALL | PV below SP-07 | High | Check the trip. Do not reset until PV is above SP-06. |
| PT deviation | Difference above SP-11 for T-07 | Medium | Check the transmitters. |
| PT fault | Either transmitter bad | Medium | Repair the transmitter. |
| PV-512 open | Position above SP-13 for T-09 | Medium | Check the flare. Check the compressor load. |
| Flare not proven | Flare status false | High | Check the flare pilot. |
| K-501 trip | State is Tripped | High | Find the cause. Reset after repair. |
| Anti-surge active | Signal true for T-08 | Medium | Check the suction flow. Check the load. |
| Serial comms loss | No data for T-10 | Medium | Check the link. |
| PIC-510 in Manual | Mode is Manual | High | Return PIC-510 to Auto. |

**6.2.9 Abnormal handling**

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-TPC-030 | If one of PT-501A/B is bad, the BPCS uses the other. If both are bad, the BPCS sets load demand to SP-12 and closes PV-512. It raises a high priority alarm. | FAT: fail transmitters |
| FR-TPC-031 | PV-512 fails closed on loss of air or signal. The tank PSV protects against overpressure in that case. | FAT: remove signal |
| FR-TPC-032 | Load demand goes to the minimum on loss of signal. | FAT: remove signal |
| FR-TPC-033 | The hardwired run, trip and ready signals are the basis for interlocks. Serial data is for display only. On serial comms loss, the BPCS raises an alarm and keeps the last state. | FAT: remove the link |
| FR-TPC-034 | The BPCS does not restart compressors by itself after a power loss. All compressors go to Tripped. The operator resets and starts them. | FAT: power cycle |
| FR-TPC-035 | After a restart, PIC-501 output starts at the minimum load. PIC-510 output starts at zero. Both controllers start in Auto. | FAT: power cycle |
| FR-TPC-036 | Anti-surge is provided by the vendor package. The BPCS receives the anti-surge active signal and the vendor trip signal. It does not command the anti-surge valve. | FAT: simulate signals |

**6.2.10 Operator interface**

The operator sees:
- PV, setpoints and outputs of PIC-501 and PIC-510.
- The state of K-501A/B and the lead selection.
- The position of PV-512.
- The flare status.

The operator changes:
- SP-01.
- The lead selection.
- The mode of PIC-501.

The operator gets these prompts:
- "Push START on the K-501 faceplate."
- "Use local stop on K-501."
- "Push RESET after you find the trip cause."

Operations must sign off on states and prompts (OI-07).

**6.2.11 Open items**

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Confirm compressor type and capacity control method | Mechanical lead | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-02 | Define the tank high-high and low-low SIFs and the bypass method in the SRS | Safety engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-03 | Decide on a make-up gas source for vacuum protection | Process engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-04 | Confirm all provisional values in 6.2.3 and 6.2.8 | Process engineer with Operations | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-05 | Confirm the PV-512 fail position and the rule for an unproven flare | Process and safety engineers | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-06 | Confirm the load demand signal is hardwired | Integrator | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-07 | Operations sign-off on states and prompts | Operations manager | 2026-12-04 |
| OI-08 | Assign transmitter tags and the tank tag in the instrument index | Instrument lead | 2026-11-06 |

I assumed that PIC-510 modulates, that the load demand is a hardwired analog signal, and that PV-512 fails closed. I could not check these from the text. Each is covered by an open item.
